outcome.from: Moratorium proposal withdrawn November 19, 2025. The Lansing Zoning Board of Appeals ruled on December 23, 2025 that the proposed AI/HPC data center is a permitted "general processing" use under existing industrial/research zoning; Cayuga Lake Action Now (CLEAN) and FLX Strong filed an Article 78 petition in NY State Supreme Court on January 30, 2026 against the Lansing ZBA and TeraWulf challenging that ruling. The outcome of the Article 78 petition was not confirmed as of this pass (2026-07-31); the last located update was an April 14, 2026 report on a separate state water-permit approval for the associated power plant, which could not be accessed this pass due to source rate-limiting.
outcome.to: Moratorium proposal withdrawn November 19, 2025. The Lansing Zoning Board of Appeals ruled 3-2 on December 22, 2025 that the proposed AI/HPC data center is a permitted "general processing" use under existing industrial/research zoning; FLX Strong and Cayuga Lake Environmental Action Now (CLEAN) filed an Article 78 petition in NY State Supreme Court on January 29, 2026 against the Lansing ZBA, TeraWulf, and its subsidiary Lake Hawkeye, challenging that interpretation. On 2026-04-29, Tompkins County Supreme Court Judge Mark Masler denied respondents' motion to dismiss, ruling that petitioners' alleged noise/environmental harms were not speculative and ordering ZBA/TeraWulf to answer by May 22, 2026. As of a September 9, 2026 report, the Article 78 suit remained pending with no reported ruling on the merits. Separately, and independent of any Town of Lansing action, NY Governor Hochul's July 14, 2026 Executive Order 62 (a one-year pause on state discretionary permits for data centers of 50 MW or more) currently affects the project, which TeraWulf's own SEC filings describe as scaling toward roughly 300-750 MW at this site.
outcome.reason: Updates the litigation timeline with the confirmed December 22, 2025 ZBA vote date, January 29, 2026 filing date, the April 29, 2026 denial of the motion to dismiss, and the still-pending status of the suit as of September 2026, plus the intervening state-level Executive Order 62 pause, none of which were resolved in the prior pass.

evidence.title: Enfield Readies, Newfield Adopts Data Center Moratorium
evidence.publisher: Bob Lynch, Enfield Councilperson (blog, first-hand meeting account)
evidence.supports: First-hand account of the July 9, 2026 Newfield Town Board meeting, naming the exact law title, confirming the unanimous vote, and describing the public hearing.
evidence.quote: What the Newfield Town Board adopted July 9 was a “Local Law Imposing a Temporary Town-Wide One Year Moratorium on Data Processing Centers.” The Newfield Board's vote was unanimous.

new_candidates.date_enacted: Not yet enacted as of 2026-09-23. On 2026-05-13 the Town Board adopted a resolution directing the Planning Board to draft data center legislation. A draft moratorium local law (modeled on Newfield's) was rewritten twice between July and mid-August 2026 on the advice of Town legal counsel Guy Krogh. At its August 12, 2026 meeting the Town Board did NOT set a public hearing as previously expected; it instead held off action, pushing back the hearing and the law's adoption to October 2026 at the earliest.
new_candidates.duration: Proposed as a one-year moratorium in the draft local law circulating as of July-August 2026.
new_candidates.legal_basis: May 13, 2026 Town Board resolution directing the Planning Board to draft data center legislation; a subsequent draft local law (closely modeled on Newfield's adopted moratorium) grew from three to eight pages through successive rewrites by Town legal counsel Guy Krogh between July and August 2026. No public hearing had been set and no adoption vote had occurred as of 2026-09-23.
new_candidates.trigger: Preemptive; no data center has been proposed in Enfield, but officials cited the town's lack of zoning, limited water and electric infrastructure, concern that 'satellite data centers' could arise near TeraWulf's proposed Lansing project, and the regional wave of moratoria (notably Newfield's) as reasons to act.
new_candidates.current_status: Pending as of 2026-09-23, and delayed. A councilperson's first-hand August 2026 account of the August 12, 2026 Town Board meeting states the Board 'held off action, postponing the process for at least a month and pushing off any hearing and the law's adoption until October at the earliest,' citing unresolved legal concerns raised by Town counsel Guy Krogh about the Newfield-modeled draft. No hearing date or adoption has been confirmed as of this pass.
new_candidates.outcome: As of this pass, Enfield has directed its Planning Board/Town Attorney to draft a one-year data center moratorium local law, but the Town Board postponed setting a public hearing at its August 12, 2026 meeting over legal counsel's concerns, pushing adoption to October 2026 at the earliest; no vote had occurred as of 2026-09-23.

At its September 15, 2026 meeting the Town Board unanimously voted to have Town Attorney Benjamin Gailey draft a proposed local law establishing a data center moratorium; the drafted law will need its own public hearing before adoption. No hearing date had been set and no local law had been adopted as of this pass.
